operations_plan.summary: Add an external circumferential chamfer to the lower edge of the largest smooth cylindrical section of the cylindrical heat-break tube, matching the size and angle of its existing upper-edge chamfer. Preserve the axial bore, overall length, reduced lower stem, threads, shoulders, and all other solids.

steps.description: Isolate solid 3, the Cylindrical heat-break tube, from the exploded assembly. Confirm that the target is the largest-diameter smooth external cylinder visible above the reduced-diameter threaded lower shank. Do not select the heater block, nozzles, split clamp, or any cold-side housing components.

Interrogate the existing external chamfer at the top circular rim of the largest smooth heat-break cylinder. Retrieve its chamfer definition from the B-rep or measure its two setbacks and included angle from the adjacent terminal annular face and the main cylindrical face. Use this existing top chamfer as the sole dimensional reference; because no numerical value is supplied, retain the measured/reference-linked value rather than introducing an arbitrary chamfer size. Exclude any internal bore lead-in or top-bore cone from the measurement.

Locate the complete external circular edge at the lower end of the same largest-diameter smooth cylinder, where that cylinder transitions toward the reduced-diameter lower stem/threaded section. Resolve the edge topologically as the boundary shared by the main smooth cylindrical exterior and its lower annular shoulder or transition face. Confirm that the selected edge is external, continuous through 360 degrees, and coaxial with the heat-break axis. Do not select an edge of the axial filament bore, a thread crest, thread runout, or the bottom end of the threaded shank.

Apply a subtractive edge-chamfer operation to the resolved lower external circumferential edge. Set the chamfer to exactly match the existing top external chamfer: copy its setback distance and angle, or use an equal/same-size linked chamfer constraint if supported by the CAD system. Orient the chamfer so that it removes only the sharp lower outside corner and creates a lead-in from the reduced lower region onto the largest cylindrical locating surface. Keep the main cylinder diameter unchanged away from the chamfer and do not change the axial position of the existing shoulder or the overall component length.

Regenerate solid 3 and verify that the largest smooth cylinder now has matching upper and lower external chamfers. Check that the new chamfer is concentric with the heat-break axis, forms a continuous annular lead-in, and does not break through to the axial filament passage. Compare the edited body with the original to confirm that only minimal material at the lower outer rim was removed and that the axial bore, thermal neck, reduced-diameter stem, external threads, shoulders, end faces, and overall length remain unchanged. Confirm that solids 0, 1, 2, and 4 through 8 are unmodified and that the new lead-in improves insertion into the mating bore without changing the nominal cylindrical fit beyond the chamfer.
